description: EverOS memory server run (add, flush, search), exported by its built-in OTLP/HTTP observability.
notes: everos[otel] 1.7.0 (IN9.6) runs as its server from a work directory whose root folder holds its EVEROS_ROOT state (everos init) and the XDG and TMPDIR directories, so a run writes nothing outside the scenario folder; the pinned environment is the uv tool project tools/capture/everos (the binary under CETRA_CAPTURE_TOOLS, the o200k_base tokenizer pre-seeded in TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR by fetch-tools). The LLM and embedding endpoints are the mock (EVEROS_LLM__BASE_URL / EVEROS_EMBEDDING__BASE_URL), the model name is LiteLLM-style openai/gpt-4o-mini, embeddings answer 1024 dims (EVEROS_EMBEDDING__DIM), and EVEROS_OBSERVABILITY__ENDPOINT is the receiver's full traces URL with capture_content on. Every chat request carries the same fixed JSON answer, which validates only the boundary task's Reply model (IN9.6 step 4: the mock ignores response_format), so add succeeds, flush's episode and summary extraction fail validation (two attempts each, LLMCallError error spans) and search answers an empty episode list. EverOS's requests declare no tools, so they take the scripted chat turns in arrival order; the four extraction attempts run two-by-two in a background job whose order varies between runs, which is harmless because every chat turn carries the same answer. The startup embedding probe (a dimension check) takes the first embeddings turn and the search's query embedding the last, after a 2 s drain keeps it behind the extraction attempts. Expected: everos.memory.add (span, session id) with everos.memcell.boundary (llm, 262/24 tokens, cost none: the openai/ prefix is not priced), everos.memory.flush (span) with the failed extraction spans, everos.memory.search (retriever, user id, input and output since capture_content is on) with everos.search.recall, everos.embedding (embedding, 5 input tokens, cost computed: text-embedding-3-small is priced) and everos.search.rank, plus everos.ome.extract_agent_case (agent, the strategy that skips: the message has no assistant turn) and, on the failed extractions, error statuses with LLMCallError exception events whose stacktraces name the installed package's scrubbed path. The episode and summary spans sum both attempts (524/48). EverOS mints a request id per API call, a memcell id per cut and a run id per strategy run; all three are volatile. No telemetry leaves the process: the mock and the receiver are the only hosts.
